description:
FILED s470bn (Opus, 2026-09-05) from the round-27 ranked table
(docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Â§A.4.3).

`moo-objs` is 36-55x perl and is the OO macro row, so its profile is the one
that should rank method dispatch, `bless`, accessor calls and argument passing.
It does not.  Measured (sb-sprof, :cpu, 1 ms, 22 655 samples at N=60 000):

  * `pcl:p-use` had TOTAL 59.7 % of the samples â the Moo LOAD, i.e. task
    #1188's constant seen from inside;
  * with Moo pre-`p-use`d out of the profiled region, 16 % is still SBCL's own
    compiler (`sb-c::*`: the program is loaded as SOURCE, because a program
    containing `use M` cannot be compile-file'd first â the p-use sits in an
    eval-when and runs before the plain load-time `(setf @INC â¦)`);
  * what remains is package and CLOS machinery, not object work:
    `list-all-packages` under a system mutex 17.9 %, `sb-kernel:%member-eq`
    12.6 %, `package-implements-list` 4.3 %, `sb-pcl` BRAID 5.1 %,
    `shared-initialize` 4.0 %, `update-ctors` 2.6 %, plus ~10 % of thread locks.
    The graph attributes these to `sb-impl::%defpackage` (11.4 %) and
    `sb-pcl::call-with-ensure-class-context` (12.2 %).

WHAT IS OWED: an instrument that measures the LOOP alone.  Two shapes, both
cheap: (a) profile at two N and subtract per function (the honest one);
(b) load the class from a separate already-loaded module so the profiled region
contains only the constructions.  The half-built (b) is
`scratch/s470bn/prof2.pl`, which pre-`p-use`s named modules and injects the
program's own `@INC`/`*pcl-pl2cl-path*` preamble lines into the driver (both
were needed: `@INC` for the load, the pl2cl path because Moo's own load does a
string eval).  It still leaves the 16 % compile share.

DO NOT re-derive: the bench row's `t(N) - t(0)` DOES subtract the module load,
so `moo-objs`' 2.4 s at N=20 000 (120 us per iteration against perl's 2.2 us)
is loop time and the 54x is real.  What is missing is only the BREAKDOWN.


=== DONE (s473r, 2026-09-07) â the instrument, the table, and a lever out of it ===

THE INSTRUMENT is shape (a), the one this task called "the honest one":
profile at N and 2N with the module pre-`p-use`d (s470bn`s prof2.pl, re-rooted)
and SUBTRACT per function.  Everything constant â the Moo load AND the 16 %
that is SBCL compiling the program â cancels, so no surgery is needed for the
compile share either.  Tools left behind in the s473r worktree:
`scratch/s473r/prof2.pl`, `scratch/s473r/profdiff.pl`, `scratch/s473r/count.pl`
(the encapsulating counter below).

THE TABLE (N=20000 -> 60000, sb-sprof :cpu 1 ms, self-count deltas
renormalised over the positives):

    14.8 %  (flet with-system-mutex-thunk :in list-all-packages)
     4.5 %  call-with-recursive-lock
     4.0 %  sb-kernel:%sxhash-string
     3.9 %  sb-kernel:%member-eq
     3.5 %  sb-pcl BRAID
     3.3 %  sb-ext:package-implements-list
     2.5 %  shared-initialize
     1.5 %  the program`s OWN subs (the only PCL-emitted frame in the top 20)
    graph: sb-pcl::call-with-ensure-class-context 24.4 % TOTAL,
           sb-impl::update-package-with-variance 14.8 %

SO THE ANSWER TO THE TASK`S QUESTION IS NEITHER OF THE TWO IT EXPECTED.  It
is not the call protocol (A.2 row 7 â the frame does not appear at all), and
it is not the method/overload cache (#582) or %sxhash-string (4.0 %, and it
is the eval cache`s key, not a hash-key stringification).  It is the PACKAGE
PREAMBLE, re-run.  Counted, not inferred â `sb-int:encapsulate` on
ensure-class / %defpackage / ensure-class-using-class / make-package, at two
N, differenced:

    per moo-objs ITERATION:  12 x defpackage  and  12 x ensure-class
      10 of each: Method::Generate::Accessor::_Generated (Moo`s Sub::Quote
                  eval package)
       2 of each: Pt

Every emitted program opens with the package preamble for the packages it
mentions, and the program a STRING EVAL produces is an emitted program.

SHIPPED FROM IT (commit 086687ea, runtime only): `p-defpackage` runs CL`s
`defpackage` only when `%p-package-ready-p` says the package is not already
there with `(:use :cl :pcl)`.  moo-objs **1.9986 -> 1.2193 s, B/A +63.9 %,
38.15x perl -> 29.59x**; methret +3.1 % and json-rt -0.7 % as controls;
`use Moo; print 1` 0.036 -> 0.033 s end to end, so t(0) barely moves and
s473p`s t(N)-t(0) trap is not hiding anything.

FILED FROM IT: **#1518** â the same preamble`s `(defclass plc-x () ())`,
which pl2cl writes literally and which the runtime therefore cannot guard.
It carries the post-fix table (sb-pcl machinery, ~35 % of the loop, nothing
above 4.6 %), the guard design (compare DIRECT SUPERCLASSES, not existence)
and the full-boat bar.

A.2 ROW 7 IS NOT SIZED AND SHOULD NOT BE, on this evidence: the call protocol
is invisible in moo-objs` loop profile both before and after.  Whoever takes
row 7 needs a different row â `methret` or `subret` â and should say so.
subject: the moo-objs macro row cannot be profiled as object work: p-use was 59.7 % of its samples and SBCL compile is 16 % - an instrument that separates load from loop is owed
